chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, and from 'Ali ibn Hadid and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: A man stepped on excrement and his foot sank into it. Does that invalidate his wudu (ablution), and is washing it obligatory upon him?
He said: “He does not wash it unless he considers it filthy; rather, he wipes it until its trace goes away, and he prays.”

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: if najasah reaches his waistband or his sock, there is no impediment to praying in them, because they are among the things with which salat (prayer) is not complete by themselves, unlike other clothing besides them. This indicates that.

key_terms.أَثَرُهَا: its trace; the remaining sign of the impurity
key_terms.تِكَّتَهُ: his waistband; a small worn item mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.جَوْرَبَهُ: his sock; another small worn item mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.عَذِرَةٍ: excrement; impure filth stepped upon in the ruling discussed
key_terms.نَجَاسَةٌ: ritual impurity; impure substance affecting garments
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution); the ritual state being asked about
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهَا: he washes it; referring to washing the affected foot or area
key_terms.يَمْسَحُهَا: he wipes it; removing the trace without full washing in this case

ai.seo_question: Does stepping on excrement invalidate wudu and require washing before prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning contact with najasah and its effect on wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer). It states that stepping on excrement does not invalidate wudu, and that certain small garments affected by najasah do not prevent the validity of prayer.
